heroHeadline: Miami Jury Convicts Four in Moïse Assassination; Artibonite Displacement Surges as Viv Ansanm Holds Gains; BINUH Reports 1,642 Killed in Q1 2026
heroSubtitle: On May 8, 2026, a Miami federal jury convicted all four defendants — Arcángel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages — on five counts in the conspiracy to assassinate President Jovenel Moïse, marking the first US criminal accountability for the July 7, 2021 killing that triggered Haiti's governance collapse; all face potential life sentences with sentencing set for late summer 2026, though higher-level Haitian masterminds remain unindicted and free. Simultaneously, UN BINUH released its Q1 2026 report documenting at least 1,642 killed and 745 injured in Haiti from January through March 2026 — a pace that annualizes to 6,500+ deaths for the full year, which would exceed 2024's record toll of 5,600+. IOM Emergency Tracking Tool 92 (ETT-92) confirms a fresh displacement wave of 4,419 individuals (1,166 households) from Petite-Rivière de l'Artibonite and Dessalines between May 2–7, as Viv Ansanm maintains territorial gains from the March–April offensive that killed 16–70 people in Jean-Denis and displaced 13,500+. PM Fils-Aimé continued his May 8–11 diplomatic mission to Rome and the Vatican — drawing criticism from Haitian media that gangs are advancing while the PM accumulates foreign trips — while the GSF advance force of ~545 personnel remains exclusively focused on Port-au-Prince, leaving Artibonite without international security support. The US Supreme Court's ruling on TPS (Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot) affecting approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders remains pending after April 29 oral arguments, with a decision expected by late June or early July 2026. Haiti's August 30 election schedule remains in serious jeopardy: no electoral decree issued, voter registration not yet begun, 23 communes inaccessible, and gang control of Port-au-Prince estimated at 80–90%.
